title: VPC hybrid tiling & safety buffer matrix (working)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sheet to explore a hybrid tiling approach for Private/VPC deployments and quantify safety buffer (spare) requirements across three region types (EDGE, REGIONAL, CORE). Goal is to provide a compact matrix that links topology choices -> utilization assumptions -> BOM (GPU/node counts) -> procurement phasing and spare rotation policy.

High-level assumptions (TL;DR):
- Target steady-state global RPS: 120k requests/day for customer X (mixed chat+batch).
- Latency-sensitive lane (L-lane) target: p95 < 120ms for 512-token requests.
- Batch/throughput lane (B-lane) target: throughput elasticity, 8–16x batching.
- Typical model: 27B variant quantized (approx 24GB vRAM effective after quant and KV overhead).
- Candidate GPUs: A100-40GB, A10G, and H100-80GB for CORE; heterogeneous mix allowed per-region.
- Node config: 2x GPUs per server for high-availability; rack=42U, 20 nodes/rack (tight mix).
- Utilization target for planning: 60% for CORE, 45% for REGIONAL, 30% for EDGE (to keep headroom for spiky latency).

Key idea (hybrid tiling):
- Tile on two axes: workload (L-lane vs B-lane) and region (EDGE/REG/CORE).
- Keep small, highly-available L-lane pools in EDGE/REG for sub-100–150ms needs (more nodes, lower per-node utilization).
- Consolidate B-lane to CORE and regional batch pools; use autoscaling for burst.
- Safety buffer expressed as percent of active pool + discrete spare GPUs (rotating) to cover HW failures and urgent expansion.

Scenarios (quick):
- Scenario 1 (latency-first): More L-lane capacity in REGIONAL, conservative utilizations.
- Scenario 2 (cost-first): Shift more batch to CORE, higher utilization assumptions, smaller EDGE pools.
- Scenario 3 (balanced): Moderate L-lane in REG, split batch across CORE+REG with 20% spare buffer.

Matrix (summary table):
Region | Primary role | GPU type recommended | Active GPUs | Utilization target | Spare buffer (%) | Spare GPUs (rounded)
CORE   | B-lane / consolidation | H100-80GB (preferred) | 320 | 60% | 18% | 58
REGION | L-lane + B-hybrid      | A100-40GB              | 160 | 45% | 22% | 35
EDGE   | L-lane (latency)       | A10G                    | 48  | 30% | 30% | 15

Notes on the numbers above: active GPUs are a starting point for the customer's projected peak month. Spare buffer computed as a combination of % headroom + 1-2% discrete for immediate hot-swap. We bias edge spare % higher because replacement lead time is longer in remote colo.

Node / rack translation (estimates):
- Assume mix: CORE=H100 single-slot (2 GPUs per node) -> CORE nodes = ceil(320 / 2) = 160 nodes -> racks = ceil(160 / 20) = 8 racks.
- REGION nodes = ceil(160 / 2) = 80 nodes -> racks = 4 racks.
- EDGE nodes = ceil(48 / 2) = 24 nodes -> racks = 2 racks (spread across 3 colos).
- Total racks baseline = 14 racks. Spare GPU pool requires additional 20 GPUs staged across CORE/REGION/EDGE (we include these in spare GPUs above).

BOM quick estimate (unit-level):
- H100-80GB GPUs: 320 active + 30 spare = 350 units -> GPU list price est: $30k -> GPU capex ~ $10.5M (list).
- A100-40GB GPUs: 160 active + 40 spare = 200 units -> $12k -> ~$2.4M.
- A10G GPUs (edge): 48 active + 15 spare = 63 units -> $3k -> ~$189k.
- Servers (dual-GPU nodes): CORE 160, REGION 80, EDGE 24 -> total 264 nodes -> avg server cost $18k -> server capex ~ $4.75M.
- Networking + switches + PDUs + racks + cold aisle infra estimate: per-rack avg $110k -> 14 racks -> $1.54M.
- Total ballpark capex (list prices, pre-negotiation): ~$19.4M. (remark: huge variability — this is intentionally coarse)

Procurement phasing (recommended):
- Phase 0 (0–3 months): Acquire single CORE rack (test H100 tiles) and 2 regional racks for pilot. Validate tiling, autoscaler hooks, KV caching across topology.
- Phase 1 (3–9 months): Bulk buy for CORE to reach 60% of target, plus one spare rotation crate (pre-staged).
- Phase 2 (9–15 months): Fill REGION and EDGE pools, begin swap schedule for spares, formalize cross-region fallback routes.

Safety & spare policy (working rules):
- Hot spares: keep 10% of active GPUs as “hot” in hot-swap servers (racked, cabled, pre-configured) distributed across CORE/REGION.
- Cold spares: additional 5–10% kept as cold inventory in nearby warehouses for EDGE region with longer lead times.
- Rotation cadence: cycle spares into active pool on a 9–12 month cadence to exercise hardware and update firmware.
- Replacement SLA: 48–72 hrs for CORE/REGION, 5–7 days for EDGE if dependent on shipping.

Power/cooling notes (ops):
- H100 pods assume 6–9kW per server under peak; power budget per rack should be planned conservatively at 30kW.
- Evaluate rack-level breakers and PDU overhead; include 15% headroom for future procured waves.

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- [ ] Confirm model memory footprint for the customer sample prompts (Maya -> run evals with model-team).
- [ ] Validate continuous-batching behavior and effective throughput per GPU on A10G/A100/H100 (Diego + serving-runtime bench).
- [ ] Finalize procurement discount assumptions with Finance (Priya). Current BOM uses list prices; target 20–30% off list for RFP.
- [ ] Decide spare distribution policy: more hot spares in CORE vs cold spares for EDGE? (Ops workshop).
- [ ] Add failure-rate historicals to tune spare % (SRE to pull 24-month telemetry).

Edge-case scenarios and sensitivity (short notes):
- If actual utilization needs to be 75% in CORE (cost pressure), we can reduce total GPUs by ~12–15% but that increases outage risk and reduces ability to absorb sudden RPS spikes; recommend negotiated overcommit SLA for cost-first customers.
- If procurement lead times extend beyond 90 days, bump EDGE cold spares to 40% of active pool until supply chain normalizes.

Appendix: compact capacity formulas (for the sheet)
- active_gpus_required = ceil( (expected_peak_tokens_per_sec * avg_tokens_per_request) / (gpu_tokens_per_sec_at_target_latency) )
- nodes_required = ceil(active_gpus_required / gpus_per_node)
- racks_required = ceil(nodes_required / nodes_per_rack)
- spare_gpus = max(ceil(active_gpus_required * spare_pct), discrete_minimum_spares)

Quick calc example (CORE B-lane):
- assumed gpu_tokens_per_sec_at_target_latency (H100) = 420 toks/sec (512 token window amortized) -> need 120k/day ~= 1.39 toks/sec avg -> due to burstiness assume 15x peak factor = 20.8 toks/sec -> GPUs required ~= ceil(20.8 / 420) = 1 per throughput bucket -> scaled across customer buckets -> yields the 320 active GPUs estimate after applying product-level concurrency multipliers and multi-model overhead. (This is intentionally sketchy — benching needed)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working document. Numbers are intentionally conservative for EDGE and more aggressive in CORE. Please add comments inline on Confluence page linked above or add tickets under JIRA-PLAT-2345.
- If we decide to push quantized 4-bit variants heavily, expected GPU counts will drop but we must re-evaluate perf/latency trade-offs and KV cache impacts.

End of sheet.

Revision history quick:
- 2026-01-14: initial draft (Maya)
- 2026-02-02: updated with A100/H100 pricing mockups (Priya)
- 2026-02-18: added node/rack translation and spare policy (Diego)
